question: Over the last few days, Veneto has been struck by extreme weather events, with between 150 and 246 ml of rain descending in just two days. This has caused considerable damage, particularly in the provinces of Vicenza and Padua, forcing the region’s governor to declare a state of emergency.

The worst of the damage is thought to have occurred after a number of rivers and streams burst their banks, flooding towns and cities and bringing road and rail transport to a standstill – despite the due countermeasures taken. The number of rescue operations carried out has already reached 80.

In view of this, can the Commission say whether it intends to support the region and all the local entities hit by this wave of extreme weather events by activating the European Union Solidarity Fund in good time?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (17.4.2024) The EU Solidarity Fund (EUSF)1 can only be activated at the request of Italy, which has a deadline of 12 weeks as from the occurrence of the first damage, demonstrating that the total direct damage exceeds the thresholds specified in Article 2 Regulation (EC) No 2012/2002.

The EUSF may cover a part of the costs for emergency and recovery operations incurred by public authorities. This means, for example, the recovery of essential infrastructure, provision of temporary accommodation to the population, cleaning-up operations, and protection of cultural heritage. Private damage is not eligible.

Additionally, Veneto plans to invest EUR 42 million under its 2021–2027 European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) programme in measures to adapt to climate change and prevent and manage climate related risks such as: floods and landslides (including awareness raising, civil protection and disaster management systems, infrastructure and ecosystem-based approaches), risk prevention and management of non-climate related natural risks (for example, earthquakes), and risks linked to human activities (for example, technological accidents), including awareness raising, civil protection and disaster management systems, infrastructures and ecosystem based approaches.

Finally, the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development (EAFRD) supports investments in the restoration of agricultural production potential damaged by natural disasters and adverse climatic or catastrophic events under the Italian common agricultural policy (CAP) Strategic Plan 2023-2027, as well as risk management tools (including for risks of extreme weather events).
EAFRD also foresees a similar measure under the Italian Rural Development Programme 2014-2022.
1 Council Regulation (EC) No 2012/2002 of 11 November 2002 establishing the European Union Solidarity

Fund (OJ L 311, 14.11.2002, p. 3) as amended by Regulation (EU) No 661/2014 of the European Parliament and the Council of 15 May 2014 (OJ L 189, 27.6.2014, p. 143) and by Regulation (EU) 2020/461 of the European Parliament and the Council of 30 March 2020 (OJ L 99, 31.3.2020, p. 9). https://eurlex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:32002R2012
